 Number of flood victims in Selangor increases, reduces in Perak
 Wednesday, 18 Nov 2026
 | 10:55 AM MYT

 KUALA LUMPUR: The number of evacuees in flood-hit states has risen to 2,485 this morning, up from 2,231 yesterday evening, following an increase in the number of victims in Selangor and the opening of two relief centres (PPS) in Negri Sembilan.
 In SELANGOR, the number of flood victims has increased to 1,373 people from 363 families this morning, up from 1,111 people from 295 families yesterday evening, who are currently accommodated at 10 PPS.
 According to the Social Welfare Department’s (JKM) 'InfoBencana' portal, the PPS at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Dato' Maharaja Lela has the highest number of flood victims, totalling 355 people, followed by SK Parit Mahang (343), Sekolah Rendah Agama (SRA) Bukit Kuching (182), Dewan Masjid An-Naim Kampung Jalan Kebun (182) and KAFA Integrasi Hidayah Bukit Cherakah (115).
 Others are at the PPS at Dewan Orang Ramai Bukit Kuching Tengah (85), Dewan Orang Ramai Seri Harmoni (63), SRA Batu 8 Ijok (25), SK Batu Arang (12) and Dewan MPPK Kampung Permatang Kundang (11).
 In PERAK, the number of victims at the 10 PPS in five flood-affected districts has dropped to 1,054 people (372 families), from 1,120 people (408 families) yesterday.
 The State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) secretariat reported that the Larut, Matang, and Selama district recorded the highest number of evacuees, with 617 individuals from 231 families at four PPS, followed by Kerian, with 177 evacuees from 61 families, and Manjung, with 129 evacuees from 37 families.
 In Kerian, the evacuees include 12 people, involving three families, affected by a landslide. They are at the PPS at SK Bukit Merah, the Gunung Semanggol multipurpose hall, and SK Parit Haji Aman.
 The Hilir Perak district recorded 108 evacuees from 34 families, while Kampar is sheltering 23 evacuees from nine families at the PPS at SK Kota Bharu in Gopeng.
 The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has forecast thunderstorms across all districts in Perak this afternoon.
 Meanwhile, the water level of the Kurau River at the Bukit Merah reservoir in Kerian was recorded at 9.25 metres-exceeding the danger level of 9.14 metres-while the Kampar River at Kampung Baru Kuala Dipang has surpassed the alert level, reaching 22.05 metres.
 In NEGRI SEMBILAN, two PPS have been opened in the Port Dickson district, at the Kampung Jimah Lama community hall and the Kampung Linggi community hall, to accommodate 58 evacuees from 17 families as of 8am today.
 According to data from the Social Welfare Department’s (JKM) 'InfoBencana' portal, the evacuees consist of 14 men, 16 women, and 28 children. - Bernama
